questions.statement: Which sentence uses the passive voice correctly?
questions.context: Passive voice in present and past, San Juan, grado 11, W15.

options.feedback: Correct. 'Was built' is the past passive: 'to be' in the past plus the participle of the main verb.
Incorrect. The passive requires the participle 'built', not the base form 'build', after the auxiliary.
Incorrect. 'Is built' is the present passive and does not match the date '1975', which requires the past.
Incorrect. Without 'to be' there is no passive, because the main verb stays active and has no object.

questions.explanation:
La voz pasiva se construye con el verbo 'to be' en el tiempo correspondiente mas el participio pasado del verbo principal. El agente puede omitirse cuando no es relevante o cuando ya se conoce por el contexto.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'English ____ (speak) in many countries around the world.'
questions.context: Passive voice in present simple, Ponce, grado 11, W15.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Speaks' is active voice and also does not agree with the subject 'English', which is singular.
Incorrect. After 'is', the verb takes the participle 'spoken', not the base form 'speak'.
Correct. 'Is spoken' is the present passive and describes a general practice without naming who performs it.
Incorrect. 'Are' goes with a plural subject, and 'English' is singular in this sentence.

questions.explanation:
En la pasiva de presente el auxiliar es 'is' o 'are' segun el sujeto, y el participio no cambia de forma. Los participios irregulares como 'spoken', 'written' o 'built' deben aprenderse aparte, igual que en los tiempos verbales activos.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'The bridge ____ (build) in 1998 by the municipal government.'
questions.context: Passive voice in past simple, Carolina, grado 11, W15.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Is built' is the present passive and contradicts the date '1998' in the sentence.
Correct. 'Was built' is the past passive, and the agent is mentioned at the end with 'by'.
Incorrect. The past passive requires the participle 'built', not the base form of the verb.
Incorrect. Without the auxiliary 'to be', the sentence is not in the passive voice and the verb is left without an object.

questions.explanation:
El agente de una pasiva se introduce con la preposicion 'by'. Puede colocarse al final de la oracion o intercalarse entre el auxiliar y el participio, y en ambos casos la construccion es correcta.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is correct?
questions.context: Passive voice with modals, Bayamon, grado 11, W15.

options.text: The work must finished before Friday.
options.feedback: Incorrect. In the passive with a modal, 'be' always appears between the modal and the participle.

options.text: The work must be finish before Friday.
options.feedback: Incorrect. After 'be', the verb takes the participle 'finished', not the base form.

options.text: The work is must be finished before Friday.
options.feedback: Incorrect. A modal cannot be combined with the present form of the auxiliary 'to be' in that way.

options.text: The work must be finished before Friday.
options.feedback: Correct. Modals form the passive with 'modal' plus 'be' plus participle.

questions.explanation:
La pasiva con verbos modales tiene una estructura fija: modal mas 'be' mas participio. Se aplica con 'can', 'must', 'should', 'may' y 'could', y es una de las construcciones mas frecuentes en instrucciones y normas de seguridad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Why is the passive voice often used?
questions.context: Passive voice with by-phrases, Arecibo, grado 11, W15.

options.text: To make the sentence shorter in every case.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The passive is usually longer than the active, because it adds the auxiliary 'to be'.

options.text: To avoid using the past tense.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The passive works in all tenses, which is why it exists with both 'was' and 'is'.

options.text: To show who performed the action more clearly.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Quite the opposite: the passive hides or downplays the agent, while the active emphasises it.

options.text: To focus on the action or the result rather than the agent.
options.feedback: Correct. The passive highlights the result and lets you omit the agent when it is unimportant or already known.

questions.explanation:
La eleccion entre activa y pasiva depende de la prioridad del mensaje. Cuando el agente es desconocido, irrelevante o ya conocido, la pasiva evita repetirlo y mantiene el foco en el resultado de la accion.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'These books ____ (write) by a famous Puerto Rican author.'
questions.context: Passive voice in present and past, Humacao, grado 11, W15.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Was' goes with a singular subject, and 'these books' is plural in this sentence.
Correct. 'Were written' is the past passive and agrees with the plural subject 'these books'.
Incorrect. After the auxiliary, the verb takes the participle 'written', not the base form 'write'.
Incorrect. 'Have written' is the active present perfect, not a passive, because it keeps a subject as the agent.

questions.explanation:
El auxiliar de la pasiva concuerda con el sujeto, no con el agente. Un sujeto plural exige 'were' o 'are', y uno singular 'was' o 'is', independientemente de quien haya realizado la accion.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'The decision ____ (take) yesterday afternoon by the committee.'
questions.context: Passive voice with irregular participles, Aguadilla, grado 11, W15.

options.feedback: Correct. The participle of 'to take' is 'taken', and 'was taken' forms the past passive.
Incorrect. Adding -ed to an irregular verb is not correct English, so 'taked' does not exist.
Incorrect. 'Is taken' is the present passive and contradicts the time expression 'yesterday afternoon'.
Incorrect. 'Has taken' is active, but in the passive the subject must be the object of the action.

questions.explanation:
En la pasiva el sujeto recibe la accion, mientras que en la activa lo realiza. Por eso el verbo 'to take' con el objeto como sujeto produce 'was taken' y no 'has taken', que conserva el sentido activo.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which question is correct?
questions.context: Passive voice in questions, Guayanilla, grado 11, W15.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Did' requires the base form 'open' after the auxiliary, not a participle.
Incorrect. After 'was', the verb takes the participle 'opened', not the base form 'open'.
Correct. In a past passive question, the auxiliary 'was' goes before the subject and the participle comes after it.
Incorrect. Question word order requires 'when' to open the sentence and the auxiliary 'was' to follow the subject.

questions.explanation:
En una pregunta pasiva se conserva la estructura auxiliar, sujeto y participio, y lo que se hace es colocar el elemento interrogativo delante. La pasiva no cambia el orden de palabras dentro del grupo verbal.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which verbs are NOT normally used in the passive voice?
questions.context: Passive voice with go and come, Trujillo Alto, grado 11, W15.

options.text: Verbs that describe a process, such as 'to build'.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Transitive process verbs form the passive normally, as in 'the house was built'.

options.text: Verbs whose past participle is irregular, such as 'to take'.
options.feedback: Incorrect. An irregular participle does not prevent the passive, and 'was taken' is a completely standard construction.

options.text: Verbs of movement such as 'to go' and 'to arrive'.
options.feedback: Correct. Intransitive verbs have no object that can become the subject, so they do not form the passive.

options.text: Verbs that take the auxiliary 'to be'.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Stative verbs like 'to be' or 'to seem' do not form the passive, but not because of an irregular participle.

questions.explanation:
La pasiva solo es posible con verbos transitivos, porque necesita un objeto que se convierta en sujeto. Los verbos intransitivos como 'to go', 'to arrive', 'to fall' o 'to sleep' carecen de ese objeto y no admiten construccion pasiva.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'The results ____ (announce) next Friday at the school.'
questions.context: Passive voice in present simple, Barceloneta, grado 11, W15.

options.feedback: Correct. 'Will be announced' is the future passive and fits the future date 'next Friday'.
Incorrect. Without 'be' the sentence is active, and the subject 'the results' does not perform the action.
Incorrect. After 'are', the verb takes the participle 'announced', not the base form 'announce'.
Incorrect. The passive requires the participle 'announced', not the infinitive form of the verb.

questions.explanation:
La pasiva funciona en todos los tiempos: 'is built', 'was built', 'will be built', 'has been built'. Lo unico que cambia es la forma del auxiliar 'to be', que conserva la concordancia con el sujeto.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct negative: 'The pool ____ (not / open) on Mondays.'
questions.context: Passive voice in negatives, Maunabo, grado 11, W15.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Doesn't' requires the base form 'open' after the auxiliary, not a participle.
Incorrect. 'Open' is an adjective or the base form of the verb, but the passive needs the participle 'opened'.
Incorrect. 'Wasn't' is past, but the sentence describes a present routine, so the tense should not change.
Correct. 'Isn't opened' is the negative present passive and describes the center's opening routine.

questions.explanation:
La negacion de la pasiva se hace con 'not' detras del auxiliar 'to be'. El participio se mantiene igual que en las formas afirmativas, porque la negacion afecta al auxiliar y no al verbo principal.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence places the agent correctly?
questions.context: Passive voice with by-phrases, Yauco, grado 11, W15.

options.text: was painted with a group of students
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'With' indicates the tool or material used, not the person who did the painting.

options.text: The mural was painted by a group of students.
options.feedback: Correct. The agent appears after the preposition 'by', which is the standard marker of the passive.

options.text: The mural was painted of a group of students.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Of' does not introduce the passive agent; the correct preposition is 'by'.

options.text: The mural was painted by the group students.
options.feedback: Incorrect. An article or possessive is missing with 'group'; it should be 'by a group' or 'by the group of students'.

questions.explanation:
La preposicion 'by' introduce al agente de la pasiva y es la forma estandar en ingles escrito. Otras preposiciones como 'from' o 'with' pueden indicar el medio o la herramienta, pero no-who realiza la accion.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Why do instructions often use the passive voice?
questions.context: Passive voice for processes, Cayey, grado 11, W15.

options.text: To make the instructions shorter and easier to follow.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The passive is not necessarily shorter, and it adds the auxiliary 'to be' to each sentence.

options.text: To describe the action without emphasizing the person performing it.
options.feedback: Correct. In a recipe, the focus is on the process rather than on who carries it out, and the passive reflects that.

options.text: To hide important information from the reader.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Using the passive is a matter of focus, not of deliberately hiding information.

options.text: To use fewer different verb forms in the text.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The passive keeps the same number of verb forms as the active; only the auxiliary changes.

questions.explanation:
En recetas, instrucciones de montaje y normas de seguridad, la pasiva es natural porque el proceso importa mas que la persona. El resultado es un texto en el que el foco permanece en cada etapa de la accion.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'The roof ____ (repair) several times since the hurricane.'
questions.context: Passive voice in the present perfect, San Sebastian, grado 11, W15.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Without 'been' the sentence is active, and the subject 'the roof' does not do the repairing.
Incorrect. 'Was repaired' is the past simple passive and cannot be used with the expression 'since the hurricane'.
Incorrect. After 'been', the verb takes the participle 'repaired', not the base form 'repair'.
Correct. 'Has been' plus the participle forms the present perfect passive, with 'since' as the time marker.

questions.explanation:
La pasiva del presente perfecto tiene tres piezas: 'have been' o 'has been' mas el participio. Es la construccion adecuada cuando la accion se repite desde un punto de partida pasado y el agente no se menciona.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'The problem ____ (not / see) by anyone in the meeting.'
questions.context: Passive voice with the verb to see, Camuy, grado 11, W15.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Didn't see' is active, and the subject 'the problem' cannot see anyone.
Incorrect. After 'was', the verb takes the participle 'seen', not the irregular past form 'saw'.
Correct. 'Wasn't seen' is the negative past passive, and 'anyone' appears in the agent clause.
Incorrect. 'Isn't seen' is present, but the sentence describes something that already happened at a past meeting.

questions.explanation:
En la pasiva, el sujeto de la oracion es siempre el objeto de la accion. Esa es la razon por la que 'the problem wasn't seen' tiene sentido y 'the problem didn't see' no lo tiene.

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'A new sports centre ____ (build) in our town next year.'
questions.context: Passive voice in the future, Luquillo, grado 11, W15.

options.feedback: Correct. 'Will be built' is the future passive, and the agent is omitted because it is not yet relevant.
Incorrect. Without 'be' the sentence is active, and the subject does not carry out the construction.
Incorrect. The future passive requires the participle 'built', not the base form of the verb.
Incorrect. That structure is active and expresses a plan, not a passive.

questions.explanation:
El futuro pasivo combina 'will' con 'be' y el participio. Se emplea mucho en noticias y comunicados, donde el proyecto importa mas que la empresa que lo ejecuta y esa informacion todavia no se conoce.

questions.statement: Choose the correct question: '____ the documents signed before the meeting?'
questions.context: Passive voice in questions, Toa Baja, grado 11, W15.

options.feedback: Correct. The auxiliary 'were' opens the past passive question, and the main verb stays in the participle form.
Incorrect. 'Did' is an active auxiliary and requires the base form 'sign' after it, not a participle.
Incorrect. 'Have' belongs to the present perfect, but the sentence needs the past passive.
Incorrect. 'Was' is singular and the subject 'the documents' is plural, so 'were' is the correct form.

questions.explanation:
En las preguntas pasivas el auxiliar 'to be' abre la oracion y respeta la concordancia con el sujeto. El participio se mantiene al final del grupo verbal, igual que en las afirmaciones.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which active sentence is equivalent to 'The song was written by my cousin'?
questions.context: Passive voice versus active rewriting, Naguabo, grado 11, W15.

options.text: My cousin was written the song.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The sentence mixes passive and active: the subject would both do the writing and receive the object.
Incorrect. It is the correct active form, but with the subject and object roles swapped.

options.text: My cousin is writing the song.
options.feedback: Incorrect. It is present continuous and does not express a completed past event.
Correct. Moving the agent back into subject position and the object to the end restores the active form of the sentence.

questions.explanation:
Pasar de la pasiva a la activa consiste en devolver el agente de la clausula 'by' al sujeto y devolver el objeto pasivo al lugar del objeto directo. El tiempo verbal se conserva durante todo el proceso.

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'The theft ____ (report) to the police yesterday evening.'
questions.context: Passive voice with reporting verbs, Hatillo, grado 11, W15.

options.feedback: Incorrect. The passive requires the participle 'reported' after the auxiliary, not the base form 'report'.
Correct. 'Was reported' is the past passive and describes the event without emphasizing who reported it.
Incorrect. 'Is reported' is present and contradicts the expression 'yesterday evening'.
Incorrect. 'Has reported' is active, and the subject 'the theft' cannot do the reporting.

questions.explanation:
La pasiva es habitual con verbos de comunicacion como 'to report', 'to announce' o 'to declare', porque el contenido de la informacion importa mas que quien la transmite.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'The chairs ____ (make) of wood in small factories.'
questions.context: Passive voice with the verb to make, Yabucoa, grado 11, W15.

options.feedback: Incorrect. After 'are', the verb takes the participle 'made', not the base form 'make'.
Incorrect. 'Was made' is past, but the sentence describes a general process that still holds true.
Correct. 'Are made' is the present passive, and 'of wood' indicates the material rather than the agent.
Incorrect. Without the auxiliary 'to be' the sentence is active, and 'the chairs' do not do the manufacturing.

questions.explanation:
El participio de 'to make' es 'made', una forma irregular que hay que conocer aparte. En pasiva de presente se combina con 'are' o 'is' segun el sujeto, y con 'of' se indica el material.
